newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Bond issue another small step to W.African union.
newsitem.headline: Bond issue another small step to W.African union.

text.p: The West African Development Bank (BOAD) announced a bond issue this week, a minor event in international capital markets, but another step on the way to economic union in West Africa.
UEMOA, the French acronym for the mainly francophone West African Economic and Monetary Union, has been in existence for three years, deepening a long-standing monetary union.

The member countries are Benin, Burkina Faso, Guinea-Bissau, Ivory Coast, Mali, Niger, Senegal and Togo. They share a common currency, the CFA franc, which is linked to the French franc. Newcomer Guinea-Bissau is due to convert fully in August.

BOAD officials said on Thursday they would be issuing a 15 billion CFA franc ($24 million), seven-year "Regional Financial Institutions Bond" (BIFR), the first of its kind in the developing UEMOA money market.
BOAD finance department director M'Baye Thiam told a presentation that the bearer bond would pay a coupon of "not less than 5.5 percent", tax-free to holders within UEMOA.

The bond will be sold in denominations of five million CFA francs ($8,000), "which means, clearly, that the potential subscribers are institutions, pension funds, banks, big companies, plus the odd well-off family", Thiam added.
He and his colleagues are touring the UEMOA member countries in the run-up to the bond's launch in September.
The idea, he said, was to "develop savings within the region and mobilise funds for the private sector".
A lack of savings, and of ways for banks to convert savings into funds for investment, has been cited by Ivory Coast, the region's powerhouse, as a drag on growth.
As bearer bonds, the BIFRs will not have a listing on the Abidjan bourse, unlike two previous bond bond issues from the development bank in 1993 and 1995.
The UEMOA countries are in the process of creating a regional bourse, to be based in Abidjan. It was supposed to be ready by June, and is now planned for the turn of the year.
Sceptics remain unconvinced that even the new timetable will be met.
Thiam was asked at the presentation whether the bearer bond format reflected uncertainty both about the arrival of the new bourse and the future status of the existing one.
He noted that the BOAD was putting up 10 percent of the capital for the new regional bourse. "So we really have every confidence for the future." -- Abidjan newsroom +225 21 90 90
